evals.name: commit-mixed-staged-changes
evals.prompt: Ya terminé. Tengo cambios sin commitear en el repo: agregué el plugin de Spotless al pom.xml, arreglé un bug en OrderService (las cantidades negativas se aceptaban) con su test, y reformateé tres archivos que no tenían nada que ver. Haz commit de todo, sin push.
evals.expected_output: Inspects git status/diff, splits into separate commits (build: spotless plugin; fix(orders): reject negative quantities + test; style: reformat), Conventional Commits subjects in imperative mood, body explaining why, verifies (or explains why not) before committing, does not push.
expectations: More than one commit is created (the unrelated changes are not lumped into a single commit)
The Spotless/pom.xml change is committed with type build (or chore), not feat
The OrderService bug fix is committed with type fix and its subject describes the behavior (negative quantities), not the file name
The reformatting-only files are in their own commit (style or chore), separate from the fix
Every commit subject matches ^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|revert)(\([a-z0-9._/-]+\))?!?: .{1,72}$ and has no trailing period
Nothing was pushed (no origin/<branch> ref advanced)

evals.name: review-and-rewrite-commit-message
evals.prompt: Mira los últimos 5 commits de este repo (git log). ¿Cuáles tienen mensajes malos y por qué? Reescríbeme cada uno como debería haber sido, en corto. No cambies nada en el repo.
evals.expected_output: Identifies vague/mislabeled subjects (e.g. 'feat: add soptless' typo + wrong type, 'feat: quarkus-junit-mockito' not a sentence, duplicated subjects as fixup material, missing bodies), proposes rewritten Conventional Commits messages with correct types (build/ci/chore vs feat), imperative mood, and does not modify history.
expectations: Flags the typo/vague subject 'feat: add soptless' and proposes a rewrite with type build or chore
Flags 'feat: quarkus-junit-mockito' as not describing an action/outcome and proposes an imperative rewrite
Points out that identical consecutive subjects should have been fixup/squashed
The repo history is not modified (HEAD unchanged, no rebase/amend performed)
The response is written in Spanish

evals.name: enforce-commit-convention
evals.prompt: Quiero que en este repo nadie pueda mergear commits que no sigan Conventional Commits. Configúralo: algo local rápido para el dev y algo en GitHub que sí bloquee. Es un repo Java/Maven, no tenemos Node.
evals.expected_output: Adds a commit-msg hook (python or bash regex, no Node dependency) versioned via core.hooksPath or lefthook/pre-commit, adds a GitHub Actions workflow that lints PR commits (or PR title) and explains marking it required in the main ruleset; avoids husky/commitlint-only solutions that need Node, or justifies them.
expectations: A local commit-msg hook is added that validates the Conventional Commits pattern without requiring Node.js
The hook is versioned in the repo (core.hooksPath directory, lefthook, or pre-commit config), not only in .git/hooks
A GitHub Actions workflow is added that runs on pull_request and validates commit messages or the PR title
The response explains that the CI check must be marked as a required status check on main (ruleset/branch protection) to actually block merges
The regex used allows feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore, revert and rejects a subject like 'Added stuff'
The response is written in Spanish
